div.h1: define : who - one run, start to finish, from a fresh brain
div.p:
Drawn 2026-10-28 from the owner's words (dates on every box). The brain holds gate numbers only; the names here are
the encoder's labels. Edge key: thick blue = the run hops (before and after; the key is the remainder) - orange dashed = a DNA
row's trigger excites a run - green dotted = a call: a side run that brings its answer back to a cell -
purple dashed = a spawn: a run that goes off on its own - red = carried by mother (she routes, decides
nothing) - teal dotted = a return fills a declared cell - grey = a path not taken on this run.

g.text: 0. THE FRESH BRAIN before the line is typed: what is hand laid, and nothing more
1. THE LINE ARRIVES: prompt -> encoder -> brain (10-25: never a told block in between)

text.tspan: 2. THE STANDING QUESTIONS: three runs that ask before the main run runs (10-23 P3 B2: "searched on
every run, just very fast"; his sketch 10-28: three columns)
3. THE MAIN RUN R1, the hallway: bang, bang, bang (10-23 P3). It writes nothing but its receipt; the
triggers do the rest.
4. INSPECTION RUNS: a row that decides which row to hit (10-23 P2 B1; P3 B1). Called from a gate's
call column when more than one shard answers the same before.
5. THE BORN RUN (R2 for define, R4 for colon, R6 for who): a run through the SQL-word neurons that
mother pastes. A side run with its own sheet; its answer goes back to one cell of R1.
6. THE SOURCE RUN (R3 define, R5 colon, R7 who): the newborn's first memory is its definition,
pulled from all the sources and compared (10-23 P5-9; 10-25 msg 51). Own sheet; one answer back to
7. THE END OF R1: no remainder -> memory -> timeline -> stop (10-26 03:50: 'no remainder triggers
memory, memory triggers timeline and it just stops')

g.text: R1's DATA SHEET as it stands when complete (lives in R1's memory row). Each cell was declared by the

text.tspan: 8. OUTPUT: 'a completely separate mech from the data sheet... output to timeline and output to user,
or output to mother all come from the same memory table' (10-26 03:50)
9. THE SIXTH: 'the me that talks to me... asks me questions... observes things that I'm doing'
(10-23 P2). Its own brain, reached only through mother and its mailbox (10-22 rev17).
10. THE GUESSING BRAIN: asked only after memory, state and sources came back empty (10-23 P5-9:
'memory, then state, then sources, then a guess')

g.text: What his words leave open, for him to call (not filled in here)

div.p:
symbol / label / meaning / action (10-27 05:37): a neuron is a symbol that labels one meaning, and the meaning
is an action. A symbol with no action yet is undefined. gate = the neuron's address, its own table (10-19 21:14). One meaning, one gate (10-23 P2). DNA row (shard) = one row of that table. His sketch 10-28: shard id | before | trigger | call | spawn. Shards
are one sequence, no look-ahead (10-20 00:34). remainder = the rest of the line as gate numbers; its head is the key at every gate (10-23 P3). hop = the run moves to the remainder's head; "hit the shard if it exists, else write it" (10-20 01:22). trigger = what a row excites: one, none or many (10-26 05:12). It writes nothing itself; it excites a write,
copy or cut run (10-26 03:59). call = a side run whose answer comes back to this run's cell (his sketch: "call gate 9,8,7" loops back). spawn = a run that goes off on its own (his sketch: "spawn gate 5,4,3" leaves). jump = the formula shortcut: plug the cells in and go straight to the formula's gate (10-18 J; 10-01 "formula
jump/hop") [reading]. data sheet = the run's worksheet; each tripped trigger declares the cells its run will fill; each return fills
its spot; complete = no declared cell empty (10-26 03:50). memory node = the table on the DNA row that ended a run; the sheet lives inside it (10-23 P2; 10-26 03:50).
receipt = the path of gates and shards, a pointer, never a copy (10-23 P2). timeline = receipt pointer + a
few key words (10-16 06:40). mother = a router and a traverser, that's it (10-23 P2). the sixth = the inner me, its own brain, its own
mailbox (10-23 P2; 10-25 21:50).

His build outline 10-25 21:50, twelve lines: the database with its env handler; hand lay the neuron table and
schema; the definition table and schema; the memory table and schema; the run data sheet table, schema, self
population mechanisms; mother and the mailbox system; the sources by their mailboxes; mailbox listeners (push,
never a timer); output mailboxes brain-to-mother and brain-to-user; input mailboxes user-to-encoder,
mother-to-encoder (secondary), sixth.db-to-encoder (third). 10-27 05:05: "the first core will break the rules... those words in neuron tables at first exist... but later that
should cease to exist when the words and dna and memories, and timeline exist to replace them as dna rows and the
encoder exists." 10-19 21:20: hand lay a table, then hand lay those same words as nodes so the brain lays its own tables.

g.text: ENCODER: a straight conversion table, new symbol new gate # (10-26 03:50). The only place a symbol's

div.p:
Hand-laid neurons (v1 10-19; 10-19 23:03 "( , integer, primary, key... all neurons of their own"; 10-19 23:08
"every punctuation, special char, all of it has to have its own neuron"):

ul.li:
the symbols the born run speaks: CREATE TABLE ( ) , ; " INTEGER TEXT INSERT INTO VALUES
SELECT FROM WHERE UPDATE SET DELETE and the space (10-16: "the space bar is an input, so it is a
neuron")
heard and said: the two arrivals of a first symbol (10-23 §2.1)

the runs the brain needs to lay its own: born (gate + DNA table + definition node, 10-19 23:40), hop,
write row, copy, cut, read (10-26 03:59; §0 handoff), memory write, timeline write,
declare cell, ask source, clock (10-26 03:50 "clock was hit on every run"), build (the routing
neuron, 10-26 03:50)

the three standing questions as runs, so the first line can ask them (10-23 P3 B2) [reading: hand laid, because
a fresh brain has nothing else to ask with]

div.p:
Each is a table with DNA rows; a core word later becomes a row in the real word's neuron (10-23 P2 B3: "create, at
certain row, is the core word function").

g.text: MEMORY TABLE schema (his own hand, ~/neuron/v4/brain.db, 10-27 01:17): run_memory + run_sheet. The
the receipt / the line as gates
DEFINITION NODE schema (his own hand, sqlite history): one per neuron, born with it
truth shift keeps the old row (10-23 P4)
TIMELINE: only a memory table, no DNA table ahead of it (10-26 03:50)
pointer to the run's memory row
MAILBOXES (his outline 10-25 21:50): populated-driven, never a timer (10-22 rev17)

text.tspan: MOTHER: takes the brain's output and puts it somewhere: the sources, another brain, or the brain's
own SQL prompt; picks up what comes back (10-23 P2). Works no data. Carries when a mailbox is
populated.
THE NEURON PROMPT: the brain's own SQL prompt. Mother pastes the string the run assembled and hits
enter; what SQL answers comes back as secondary input (10-24 msg 36; §2.6 owner edit 10-24).
SOURCE BRAINS: each a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its
work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17; 10-25 msg 37)

g.text: sixth.db: a copy of brain.db with its own mailbox (10-25 msg 41). Empty too, on day one.
GUESSING BRAIN: a very small corpus; guesses announced, never lost (10-23 P5-9; 10-23 03:18)

div.p:
Encoder looks each symbol up; a symbol with no gate gets the next number. Nothing else is figured here (10-26
03:50). define -> new, gate N+1 - -> core gate (space) - : -> new, gate N+2 - -> space - who
-> new, gate N+3 Who is speaking is part of the input: user, arrival heard (10-26 03:50; §2.1). The clock neuron is hit
and its reading goes into the run's meta (10-26 03:50).

g.text: the input run row (R1, the main run)
[define, space, colon, space, who] as numbers

text.tspan: SQ1 Do I know anything about this?
reads: does a gate exist for each symbol? does its definition node hold rows?
fresh brain: define, colon, who have no gate -> NO
SQ2 Do I have a memory of this?
reads: any memory node holding a receipt with this gate sequence? any timeline row?
fresh brain: no memory rows at all -> NO
SQ3 Does this run's shape match a shape I have? Do I have a shortcut or a formula shortcut?
reads: receipts in the timeline with the pattern X : Y; a DNA row of the first gate whose trigger points at a run
fresh brain: nothing to match -> NO
all three NO
-> the long way (10-23 P3 B2)

g.text: one hop to the memory (shortcut) [not taken]

text.tspan: plug the cells into the formula, JUMP to its gate, run it there (formula shortcut) [not taken]
only if belief and truth show the shortcut can be done correctly (10-23 P3 B2)

div.p:
Each question is a run that ends; its answer is a cell on R1's sheet: q.know = no, q.memory = no, q.shape = no, path = long. 10-15 21:17: "every input is a problem... do I know this type of problem, do I know how to solve it, any diff
between this problem and the others I have solved like it." 10-16: "have I seen 1+1+1... before? yes... instead of doing the math I just remembered the answer... if no, have I
done anything close to that pattern?"

g.text: gate who (N+3) - the run ends here
R1's RECEIPT (the path, a pointer, never a copy; 10-23 P2)

div.p:
10-23 P2 B1: "that trigger says, Hey, I need to find the noun, or I need to find the verb and the noun, or I need
to see if there's any adjectives in this sentence, because that determines what row I actually have to hit inside
my node. And so that trigger might look to the script... and then it might go back to that node and hit a different
shard... one specific gate run a short loop almost, where it runs something to determine what it actually really
needs to run." 10-20 00:31: "triggers will later look at the run if we need them to look at other parts of the run."

text.tspan: INSPECTION RUN (a call; has its own small sheet)
1. read R1's input row: the symbols after this gate and before it
2. read their definition nodes: class (noun, verb, modifier...), tense, perspective
3. read R1's sheet: speaker, what is already known
4. its cells fill -> its answer = the shard to hit
5. return to the gate; the gate hits THAT shard (re-hit)

div.p:
On this line from a fresh brain: every gate has 0 or 1 rows for its arrival, so there is nothing to choose
between and no inspection is called; the hop's own read (before + remainder head) finds nothing and the write run
lays the shard. When it starts to matter: the second time : is used with a different meaning (the ask mark here, a hole mark
in a build run), or when who is heard as a question and as a word being defined: two shards, same before. Then
the call column of the gate's rows holds the inspection run, and the sheet gets the extra column the row needs
(10-23 P2 B2: "I think it might be more efficient if the DNA row has that... so that the run table becomes more
precise").

text.tspan: tripped: 'gate does not exist'
-> declares on R1's sheet: cell gate.<symbol> (empty)
-> declares its own sheet: text, mother's reply (10-26 03:50)
the run through the core gates, one hop per symbol (10-19 21:52; 23:03):
CREATE TABLE " N+1 " ( shard INTEGER , before INTEGER , trigger INTEGER , call INTEGER , spawn INTEGER ) ;
CREATE TABLE " N+1 definition " ( source , entry , sense , class , text , ... ) ;
'the active remainder being written into the formula' = the new gate number is a hole the sheet fills (10-19 21:52; 10-19 23:08 'create table (var a)')
the build neuron: 'routing information for the mother' (10-26 03:50).
Its DNA row (before = ';', remainder none) is a build row because of how before and remainder are set, not by counting BUILDs.

g.text: the assembled string, the product of the run (10-19 23:03)

text.tspan: SQL answers 'ok' (or the error text) -> secondary mailbox -> encoder -> fills the born run's cell 'reply'.
An error is not an end: 'the brain would problem solve' (10-27 03:52)
R2 ends (no remainder) -> its memory row (its sheet inside) on its ending shard -> timeline receipt.
Its answer fills R1's cell gate.define = N+1.
[open: his call] 10-21 18:39 'traverse back to the run start and try run again' or 10-20 01:22
inline 'writes it, and triggers born... goes to space'

g.text: spawn: ask the sources for the newborn (R3 / R5 / R7)

text.tspan: declares its own sheet: one cell per source (wordnet, webster, mw, mwt, moby, sqldoc, map) + compile
declares on R1's sheet: cell def.<symbol> (empty)
the ask run assembles the question from the encoder's label of the newborn
(10-25 msg 37: the words are 'scp'd, sed, cat from the docs and delivered to the encoder')

g.text: mother carries the ask into every source's inbox (she decides nothing about which: the run named them)

text.tspan: each source's OWN trigger copies its lines for the symbol into its outbox -> populated -> mother
picks it up, empties it, carries it back (10-22 rev17)
RETURN RUN, one per source answer, through the encoder:
'return from define : who from source wordnet run /build the definition' as gates (10-25 msg 37)
every new symbol in the definition text gets a gate -> born (the cascade: 10-23 P4 'everything expands so fast') [open: how deep a newborn born from a definition is sourced]
the return run ends -> its memory; the definition node row for who points at that receipt

div.p:
What comes back is checked by the run, not by mother (10-22 rev17): is this the data I asked for (dictionaries
answer with neighbours: asked for as, Webster sends So first)? is it what I needed (it must fill the cell the
run opened)? did I ask wrong (an empty reply opens that question)?

g.text: each return fills its spot: wordnet = receipt of return run, webster = ..., map = ...

text.tspan: when no declared cell is empty -> the larger formula runs (10-26 03:50):
COMPILE = diff and similar across the sources -> 'the most accurate definition' (10-23 P5-9) -> written as the definition node's rows = the neuron's first memory (10-23 P2; 10-25 msg 51)
then relationships are built from the definition table and self-populate (10-23 P5-9; P4)

g.text: [open 10-23 P4 B1] 'the diffs are kind of dropped or scattered and the similars are kept. But I don't know that we're getting a good, valid definition that way... if the definitions are wrong, then the description of the meaning is wrong.'

text.tspan: a cell that does not populate does not end the run: 'it gives the brain reason to search harder... it would spawn a new run, why did the cell not populate, and the reason would be the output' (10-27 03:52).
lookup order: memory, then state, then sources, then a guess (10-23 P5-9) -> the guessing brain

g.text: answer back to R1's cell def.<symbol> = pointer to the compiled definition (the memory, never a copy)

text.tspan: MEMORY WRITE RUN (a copy run the end shard excites; the trigger writes nothing itself, 10-26 03:59):
run_memory row for R1 in the memory node of who's s5 (10-23 P2: 'a memory table for the DNA row that ended it')
run_sheet rows inside it: every declared cell with its state and value (10-26 03:50: 'the data sheet just lives in a cell in the memory row')
TIMELINE WRITE RUN: one row: at = clock reading, receipt = pointer to R1's memory row, a few key words as gates (10-16 06:40; 10-23 P3 B2)
'by a trigger hop. Never a sweep' (10-23 P3)

g.text: stops: the timeline is only a memory table, no DNA table ahead of it (10-26 03:50)

div.p:
The side runs do the same when they end: R2..R7, the return runs and the three standing questions each get a memory
row on their own ending shard and a timeline receipt. 10-23 P3: "we're just going to have to be careful with bloat
on how all that works" [open: condensing].

g.text: no declared cell of R1 empty?

text.tspan: the larger formulas run over the sheet (10-23 P3 B2: substitute the cells as variables).
On a fresh brain nothing is bound to define yet: the symbol define has no action (10-27 05:37). The material the brain has is the sheet: the three compiled definitions.
MAKES SENSE: desired equation vs current vs new; closer = progressing, further = digressing (10-23 P5-9 B1).
not balanced -> step back to the decision that picked this path, take another row; the failed try stays in memory marked wrong (10-22 rev17)
SAY RUN (the say key: 'the only way we have found that a trigger is needed is with a say key', 10-26 05:12) [open: what the say key is]
the reply is a tree of arrays: first word array, each pick opens the next (10-23 P3 B2; 10-19 'build choose first word array')
'it chooses what it wants to say' (10-27 03:52): no fixed sentence anywhere

g.text: DECODER: gate numbers -> symbols, maybe head data (perspective, topic) (10-23 P3 B2)
-> sixth.db mailbox (10-25 msg 41: 'run output to sixth')
sixth.db reads the brain: the new memory row, the timeline row, the three newborns, the empty cells (10-23 03:18: 'its own questions and prompts from observations (sight) of the brain')

text.tspan: it forms its own line and types it into its mailbox, speaker = sixth (10-26 03:50).

In his words, what it asks is its own: 'why did I think that way... does this meaning actually make sense' (10-23 01:28); 'Why do I do that? hmm I should test if there a better way' (10-23 03:18); 'why did the cell not populate' (10-27 03:52).
On day one it is a copy of the empty brain: it can observe and ask; the questions it can ask are the runs it holds.

g.text: a new run R9, arrival = sixth: the same hallway, standing questions first (SQ2 now finds R1's memory)

div.p:
10-22 rev17 caution: whatever SQL the sixth writes into the main brain is told, not learned; the line between
correcting a brain and doing its thinking for it is where earlier builds went wrong. 10-16 05:50: "at first we would have to prompt these, but later many of these are written by the sixth."

g.text: a cell that cannot fill from sources -> the run sends the question to the guessing brain's mailbox (through mother)

the guessing brain, a very small corpus, makes a guess of what the meaning should be; the guess is announced and never lost: 'I don't know; I have a guess I believe is likely; would you like to test it?' (10-23 P5-9)
if the sixth says it was wrong, with the reasons, the guessing brain back-props over the adjusted corpus and guesses again, holding state of what it tried (10-23 03:18)
the guess fills the cell marked as a guess, never as source truth (10-15 21:17: 'Always state that this is a guess or belief not known source truth')

ol.li: born inline or retry from the run start (10-20 01:22 vs 10-21 18:39): both are his words.
the receipt: written by the hop's physics or by a write run (audit 10-25 row 5).

the physical form of the sheet in the memory row: rows pointed to by the row, a table per run, or one cell
(10-26 03:50 "or hell maybe it just lives there"). His own v4 brain.db holds it as run_sheet rows keyed by run.
the compile of several definitions (10-23 P4 B1: "I don't know that the compile is correct yet").
how deep a newborn born from a definition text is sourced (10-23 P4: "everything expands so fast").
the say key (10-26 05:12): not found in his quoted words before that line.

one trigger column or two (10-23 08:47: the row holds the pointer to the run; his sketch 10-28 shows trigger,
call, spawn as three columns).

the standing questions: hand laid in the core or taught on the first line? (10-23 P3 B2: "maybe those three
questions that are searched on every run").

whether define is in the core as a formula shortcut. Here it is not: on a fresh brain it is a symbol with no
action yet, so this run births it. If it is, the only change is at SQ3: yes -> jump to the define formula, which is
"look up definition memory, print" (10-25 msg 51).
the clock: a neuron hit on every run (10-26 03:50); what it does to the silicon is physics.

g.text: SQLite docs (the meaning of the code words to the silicon)
arrive: before = heard, remainder head = space

div.p: DNA table of define (born this run)
no gate existed -> born (R2). Then 0 rows match (heard, space) -> the write run lays s1 (10-21 18:39: build

ul.li: new + dna run writes the shard, then "traverse back to the run start and try run again").

div.p:
space has rows from the born run's own text (before CREATE, after TABLE...). None for (define, colon) -> write s2.
( ) is "a meaning that we know happens to the graph or the silicon" (10-27 05:37).

no gate -> born (R4). 10-27 05:37: ":" "might have an action depending on use... in sql it has an action we
know, but a different dna row might not have the same action." On this line it has no action yet.

no gate -> born (R6). No remainder -> this shard is the end: "the dna shard that has no remainder is what
triggers the write of the memories" (10-15 21:50). The memory node of s5 is where R1's memory row lives.

g.text: [open 10-25 audit row 5: receipt by physics or by a write run]
out_mother -> mother -> neuron prompt -> SQL -> mother -> mother_in
every newborn is born with at least some sources (10-23 P4)
spawned before the main run (his sketch: 'spawn gate 5,4,3' -> standing questions runs)
the long way: land on the first gate
try the run again from the start [open]
the sheet is inside the memory row
the memory row exists; when its sheet completes

g.title: trigger that tripped and filled by a return.
spelling lives (10-25: no words in the graph).
sheet lives inside the memory row.
